title: Via Panisperna to the Squash Court: Enrico Fermi and the Slow Neutron
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Via Gaeta and the Stalls of Campo de' Fiori

stops.name: Via Gaeta 19, Rome: the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Enrico Fermi is born in an apartment on Via Gaeta, a few streets from Termini station, third child of Alberto Fermi, an official of the Railways Ministry, and Ida de Gattis, a schoolteacher. The household is orderly and unliterary, thoroughly of the new Italian state, which is forty years old and still assembling itself out of the pieces of the peninsula. Neither of the family trades, the ministry and the classroom, has ever produced a physicist. The city he is born into keeps its Institute of Physics on Via Panisperna, on the Viminale hill, twenty minutes' walk away; he will be running it before he is thirty.
suggested_refs: The apartment building at Via Gaeta 19, near Termini, Rome
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'

stops.name: Rome, the death of Giulio
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month and day not established in the sources reached, defaulted to 1 January
stops.campa: His brother Giulio, a year older and the companion of his childhood, goes in for an operation on a throat abscess and does not survive it. Enrico is fourteen. The family does not recover the shape it had; the mother's grief is long and public, and the boy answers the house by leaving it for arithmetic. Physics and mathematics take the place the brother held, and he works at them with the same daily loyalty. Every biographer dates the vocation from this loss, and Fermi, who explains almost nothing about himself in writing, never contradicts them.
suggested_refs: Emilio Segre, Enrico Fermi, Physicist (1970), on the brothers

stops.name: Campo de' Fiori, the secondhand treatises
stops.date_confidence: traditional; Segre places the episode somewhere between 1915 and 1918 from family memory, with no dated record, and 1916 is chosen here only to sit the stop in sequence
stops.campa: In the market square where Giordano Bruno was burned, the book stalls sell physics and mathematics in Latin for almost nothing. After Giulio's death the boy comes with his own money and carries the volumes home, working through them alone, deriving what the text assumes and skipping nothing. The tradition, recorded by Emilio Segre out of the family's memory rather than out of any document, is that the education happened here and that the liceo is only where it was registered. He is teaching himself the physics of the previous century in the language of the Church.
suggested_refs: The book stalls of Campo de' Fiori, under the statue of Giordano Bruno

stops.name: Liceo Ginnasio Umberto I, Rome: the diploma
stops.date_confidence: year attested and the maturita falls in July; the day is not established, defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Fermi takes his classical diploma at the Liceo Ginnasio Umberto I on Via Daniele Manin, having skipped a year, at sixteen. The curriculum is Latin, Greek and Italian letters, the training that produces the country's lawyers and prefects; the physics he owns he got elsewhere and at his own expense. A plaque on the wall of the school, now the Liceo Classico Pilo Albertelli, marks the fact. In November he sits the entrance competition for the Scuola Normale Superiore, and leaves the city he was born in for the first time.
suggested_refs: The commemorative plaque at Via Daniele Manin 72, Rome

stops.name: Palazzo della Carovana, Pisa: the entrance essay
stops.date_confidence: the examination is sat in November 1918; en.wikipedia dates his entry to 1918, it.wikipedia to 1919, and the contradiction is recorded rather than resolved
stops.campa: The competition for the Scuola Normale sets the candidates an essay on the specific characteristics of sound. Fermi treats a vibrating rod, writes down the partial differential equation and solves it by Fourier analysis. He takes first place. The examiner calls him in and speaks to him as to a colleague rather than a boy of seventeen who has never left home. He enters the school in Piazza dei Cavalieri, boards with the other normalisti, and finds in Franco Rasetti the friend and collaborator of the next twenty years.
suggested_refs: The Palazzo della Carovana, Piazza dei Cavalieri, seat of the Scuola Normale Superiore
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'

stops.name: University of Pisa: the laurea at twenty
stops.date_confidence: July 1922 attested; the day is not established
stops.campa: Fermi graduates in physics at twenty with an experimental thesis on X-ray diffraction in curved crystals, work done with his own hands, since Italian physics still expects a doctorate to be made in a laboratory. The separate diploma he submits to the Scuola Normale is a mathematical paper: a theorem on probability and some of its applications. Wikipedia folds the two into one thesis; Segre's biography keeps them apart. By now he has read the German literature on quantum theory more closely than the faculty examining him has.
suggested_refs: The Pisa laurea thesis on X-ray diffraction in curved crystals, 1922

stops.name: Gottingen, the semester with Max Born
stops.date_confidence: Wikipedia gives 1923-1924 for the semester under Born; the research pool's chronology lens says 1923 and its geography lens says 1922-1923, which is impossible since he was at Pisa until July 1922; dated here to 1923 with the month defaulted
stops.campa: On an Italian government scholarship Fermi joins the institute of Max Born, where quantum mechanics is being built in argument, sentence by sentence, by men his own age. Werner Heisenberg works in the same building in these years; Robert Oppenheimer will arrive in 1926 to the same seminar ferment. Fermi is not taken up. He works at his desk, publishes, forms no close tie and goes home saying little about it. The circle that will shortly call him the Pope of physics in Rome does not notice him in Gottingen at all.
suggested_refs: Max Born's institute at Gottingen, 1923-1924
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'
robert_oppenheimer.journey.json, stop 'Gottingen: Max Born and the ferment'

stops.name: Leiden, the months with Paul Ehrenfest
stops.date_confidence: autumn 1924, roughly September to December; the arrival date is not established
stops.campa: A Rockefeller fellowship sends him to Leiden for the autumn with Paul Ehrenfest. The biographers agree that Ehrenfest's seminar, and Ehrenfest's own attention to him, mark him more than Gottingen had. What the German institute withheld, Leiden gives him: the standing to trust his own results. Ehrenfest keeps a door open toward Copenhagen and the circle of Niels Bohr, the northern network Fermi will never quite join and never quite leave. In January he takes up a teaching post at Florence.
suggested_refs: Paul Ehrenfest's house and seminar at Leiden, meeting place of the northern physics

stops.name: Arcetri, Florence: the statistics of the exclusion principle
stops.date_confidence: the Florence post runs January 1925 to late 1926 and the statistics paper is of early 1926; the month is defaulted to 01
stops.campa: On the hill of Arcetri above the Arno, a few hundred metres from the villa where Galileo died under house arrest, Fermi teaches mathematical physics and mechanics beside Franco Rasetti. Here he applies Pauli's exclusion principle to an ideal gas and works out how such particles must distribute themselves in energy. Paul Dirac reaches the same statistics months later and independently; the result carries both names. Every particle that obeys it will be called a fermion. He is twenty-four, in a provincial post, and has just written the paper that gets him Rome.
suggested_refs: The physics institute at Arcetri, above Florence
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'

stops.name: Via Panisperna, Rome: the chair at twenty-four
stops.date_confidence: the appointment is of 1926; November is taken from the academic year and the exact date is not established
stops.campa: Italy creates three chairs of theoretical physics, the first in the country. Orso Mario Corbino, director of the Institute of Physics on Via Panisperna and a senator with a talent for money, arranges that Fermi takes one of them at twenty-four. Around him gathers the group Rome will call the boys of Via Panisperna: Edoardo Amaldi, Franco Rasetti, Emilio Segre, Bruno Pontecorvo, Oscar D'Agostino, Ettore Majorana. They hand out ecclesiastical names. Corbino is Padreterno, God Almighty, who conjures posts and funds out of the state; Fermi is Il Papa, the Pope, for never being wrong.
suggested_refs: The Royal Institute of Physics on Via Panisperna, Viminale hill, Rome

stops.name: Como, the Volta congress
stops.date_confidence: the congress runs 11 to 27 September 1927 and Bohr reads his paper on 16 September; the coordinate is generic Como, since the venue was the Istituto Carducci and not, as many accounts repeat, the Villa Olmo
stops.campa: At the international congress marking the centenary of Alessandro Volta's death, Niels Bohr reads the paper that introduces complementarity to the assembled physics of Europe. Fermi is in the room, listed among the participants from Rome. He arrives known only in Italy and leaves known outside it. Werner Heisenberg and Max Born are on the same list. The argument the Como week opens is finished a month later in Brussels, where Bohr and Albert Einstein take it up in the corridors of the Solvay conference and neither of them gives way.
suggested_refs: The Istituto Carducci, Como, venue of the 1927 Volta centenary congress

stops.name: Rome, the marriage to Laura Capon
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Fermi marries Laura Capon, a university science student, daughter of an officer of the Italian navy and of a Roman Jewish family. She will write the household's account of everything that follows, from the Panisperna years to the mesa at Los Alamos, in a book called Atoms in the Family. Nella is born in January 1931 and Giulio in February 1936, the son carrying the dead brother's name. The marriage is unremarkable in the Italy of 1928; ten years later it is the single fact that decides which country gets the first reactor.
suggested_refs: Laura Fermi, Atoms in the Family: My Life with Enrico Fermi (1954)
sources: Laura Fermi, Atoms in the Family (1954)

stops.name: Villa Farnesina, Rome: the Royal Academy of Italy
stops.date_confidence: the member list is approved 13 March 1929 and Fermi's appointment dated 18 March; the Academy itself is not formally inaugurated until 28 October 1929
stops.campa: Benito Mussolini appoints Fermi to the Royal Academy of Italy, the body the regime has founded on the Via della Lungara to stand in place of the Lincei it distrusts. The seat carries the title of Excellency, a salary that roughly doubles a professor's pay, and a uniform with a feathered hat. Fermi is twenty-seven and the youngest member elected. The Academy is housed in the Villa Farnesina, directly across the street from the Palazzo Corsini where the suppressed Lincei sat, and the two doorways face each other for the length of the regime.
suggested_refs: The Villa Farnesina, Via della Lungara 230, seat of the Reale Accademia d'Italia
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'

stops.name: Rome, the party card
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Six weeks after the Academy seat, Fermi joins the National Fascist Party. The card is the price of the chair, the academy and the laboratory; most Italian professors hold one by now, and a loyalty oath will be made compulsory two years later. He is not a fascist in any sense his students can detect and he is not a resister either. He signs, keeps the salary, and builds the group. The bargain reads as ordinary in both directions until 1938, when the regime writes the racial laws and his wife becomes a category.
suggested_refs: Fermi's PNF membership, 27 April 1929

stops.name: Rome, the theory of beta decay
stops.date_confidence: a tentative paper appears in 1933 and the full paper in 1934; the name neutrino is coined in conversation around 1932, before either; the month is defaulted
stops.campa: Wolfgang Pauli has proposed an undetectable neutral particle to save the conservation of energy in beta decay, and is embarrassed by it. Fermi takes up the idea and builds the theory alone: a neutron becomes a proton, an electron and the small neutral thing are created in the interaction itself, and a new force of nature is written down with a coupling constant that still carries his name. The Italian diminutive he uses for Pauli's particle, neutrino, the little neutral one, sticks to it permanently.
suggested_refs: Fermi, Tentativo di una teoria dei raggi beta, Il Nuovo Cimento (1934)

stops.name: Rome, the report of neutron-induced radioactivity
stops.date_confidence: attested; this is the report of neutron-induced radioactivity, not of slow neutrons, which come in October
stops.campa: Irene Curie and Frederic Joliot have made light elements radioactive with alpha particles. Fermi reasons that the neutron, carrying no charge, will walk into a nucleus that repels an alpha, and starts at the bottom of the periodic table with a radon-beryllium source and a Geiger counter, working upward element by element. Fluorine answers, then aluminium, then dozens more. The report goes to La Ricerca Scientifica on 25 March. By the autumn the group has bombarded most of the table and believes, wrongly, that it has made elements beyond uranium.
suggested_refs: Fermi's note in La Ricerca Scientifica, 25 March 1934

stops.name: Via Panisperna, the paraffin wedge
stops.date_confidence: attested to 22 October 1934; the research pool's chronology lens misdates this discovery to 25 March, and the October date is the correct one
stops.campa: On the morning of 22 October, for a reason he can never afterward explain, Fermi puts a block of paraffin wax in front of the neutron source instead of the lead the plan called for. The silver target comes out a hundred times more radioactive. Hydrogen in the wax is slowing the neutrons down, and slow neutrons are swallowed by nuclei far more readily than fast ones. The group repeats the effect that same afternoon in the goldfish pond in the institute garden, water standing in for wax. The Nobel citation four years later names this day.
suggested_refs: The goldfish pond in the garden of the Via Panisperna institute
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'

stops.name: Stockholm, the Nobel ceremony
stops.date_confidence: attested; the coordinate is the canonical Konserthuset pin inherited from heisenberg.journey.json
stops.campa: Fermi takes the prize from the hand of Gustav V for the demonstration of new radioactive elements produced by neutron irradiation and for the discovery of nuclear reactions brought about by slow neutrons. He shakes the king's hand instead of giving the Roman salute, and the Italian press notes the omission. Werner Heisenberg stood on this stage five years earlier. Laura Fermi is in the hall, and under the racial laws passed in Rome that autumn she is no longer a full citizen of the country the family is in the act of ceasing to be from.
suggested_refs: The Stockholm Konserthuset, Nobel ceremony of 10 December 1938

stops.name: Southampton, the embarkation
stops.date_confidence: late December 1938; the port is given by secondary biographies (Segre 1970, Schwartz 2017) and neither port nor ship was independently verified, so the stop is a reconstruction
stops.campa: From Stockholm the family travels on, the biographies placing a few days with Niels Bohr in Copenhagen on the way, and then to England to take ship for New York. Southampton is the port the secondary accounts name; no passenger record was reached to confirm it, or the vessel. What is certain is the direction. The Nobel money stays in a bank abroad rather than being converted into lire as the currency law requires, the itinerary is arranged as a scientific trip, and the return half of it is never used.
suggested_refs: Passenger manifests of transatlantic sailings from Southampton, December 1938 (not consulted)
sources: David N. Schwartz, The Last Man Who Knew Everything (2017)

stops.name: New York, the landing
stops.date_confidence: attested; the coordinate is the canonical New York pin inherited from niels_bohr.journey.json
stops.campa: The Fermis come off the ship into New York harbour on 2 January, four of them and a Swedish bank balance, refugees whom the newspapers greet as a laureate with a family. Columbia University has the post arranged before they dock. Two weeks later Niels Bohr lands at the same water carrying in his head the interpretation Lise Meitner and Otto Frisch worked out over Christmas of what Hahn and Strassmann had found in Berlin: the uranium nucleus splits in two. The two arrivals, a fortnight apart, are the start of the American bomb.
suggested_refs: The Fermi family's arrival in New York, 2 January 1939
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'

stops.name: Pupin Hall, Columbia: the first fission in America
stops.date_confidence: attested to the night of 25 January 1939; the coordinate is corrected from the pool's 40.8075 / -73.9626 to the figures given in the Pupin Hall article
stops.campa: In the basement of Pupin Hall a team splits uranium and reads the pulses off an oscilloscope: the first nuclear fission experiment run in the United States. John Dunning, Herbert Anderson, Eugene Booth, Norris Glasoe and Francis Slack are at the bench. Fermi is a co-author and is not in the building; he is in Washington that night. The credit is routinely given to him alone and he never claims it that way. What he supplies in the following weeks is the question the experiment leaves open: how many neutrons come out, and can they be made to come back.
suggested_refs: The cyclotron basement of Pupin Physics Laboratories, Columbia University

stops.name: George Washington University, the fifth Washington conference
stops.date_confidence: the conference opens 26 January 1939; the Wikipedia article on fission does not itself name Bohr as the announcer at that session, and the coordinate is the canonical pin inherited from niels_bohr.journey.json
stops.campa: The conference on theoretical physics opens the day after the Columbia experiment, which is exactly why Fermi is here and not there. Niels Bohr has brought the fission news out of Copenhagen by way of Princeton, and the room takes it up at once; before the sessions close, physicists are telephoning their own laboratories to go and look for the pulses. Fermi and Bohr work the same corridor, the emigre and the visitor, arguing in public about what a secondary neutron would mean. Nothing is classified yet, and within a year everything is.
suggested_refs: The Fifth Washington Conference on Theoretical Physics, GWU and the Carnegie Institution, January 1939
sources: Richard Rhodes, The Making of the Atomic Bomb (1986)
niels_bohr.journey.json, stop 'Princeton and Washington, the news of fission'

stops.name: Washington, the warning to the Navy
stops.date_confidence: attested
stops.campa: Fermi is sent to the Navy Department to explain to admirals that uranium might be made to release energy in military quantities. He is heard politely and nothing follows. The government does not move until August, when Leo Szilard drives out to a cottage at Peconic on Long Island and Albert Einstein signs the letter to Roosevelt describing precisely the chain reaction Fermi came to Washington to describe in person, five months earlier. An accent and a laboratory result are not enough. A famous name on a sheet of paper is.
suggested_refs: The Einstein-Szilard letter to Roosevelt, 2 August 1939
sources: einstein.journey.json, stop 'Peconic, Long Island, the letter to Roosevelt'

stops.name: Columbia University, the graphite piles
stops.date_confidence: the Columbia exponential piles run from 1940 into 1942; the year is attested and the month defaulted
stops.campa: In the Schermerhorn and Pupin basements Fermi and Szilard build lattices of graphite bricks with uranium oxide packed into the holes, measuring how many neutrons a stack gives back for each one it swallows. Fermi stacks the bricks himself alongside the students and comes out black to the elbows. The reproduction factor climbs toward one and will not reach it. The graphite is the culprit: traces of boron in commercial carbon eat neutrons, and a purification standard has to be invented before any pile can be built. In 1942 the work moves to Chicago.
suggested_refs: The exponential graphite piles in the Columbia basements, 1940-1942
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'

stops.name: Eckhart Hall, Chicago: the Metallurgical Laboratory
stops.date_confidence: the Met Lab is organised in early 1942 and Fermi's group moves west during the spring; the month is approximate
stops.campa: Arthur Compton concentrates the scattered pile projects at the University of Chicago under a name chosen to say nothing at all: the Metallurgical Laboratory. Fermi's Columbia group moves into offices in Eckhart Hall and laboratories borrowed from a campus still teaching undergraduates. Uranium and graphite arrive by the ton, purified to a standard no industry had any reason to reach a year before. The plan is a full-size pile at a site in the Argonne forest; the contractor strikes, the site is not ready, and the pile is built where the physicists already are.
suggested_refs: Eckhart Hall, University of Chicago, offices of the Metallurgical Laboratory
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'

stops.name: Stagg Field, the pile begun under the west stands
stops.date_confidence: 16 November 1942 per the Chicago Pile-1 and Metallurgical Laboratory articles, which agree; the Enrico Fermi article alone says 6 November, and the contradiction is recorded, not resolved
stops.campa: In a doubles squash court under the west stands of the disused football field, crews under Herbert Anderson and Walter Zinn begin laying the pile: graphite bricks machined on the spot, uranium slugs pressed into the holes, layer on layer in a flattened sphere inside a timber frame. The men come off shift black as miners. The university president is not told what is being built on his campus. Fifty-seven layers go down in sixteen days, and each night Fermi computes from the day's neutron counts how many more layers will be needed.
suggested_refs: The west stands squash court, Stagg Field, University of Chicago

stops.name: Stagg Field, the pile goes critical
stops.date_confidence: attested; the coordinate is the canonical Stagg Field pin supplied by the interlock lens, which found no existing journey in the corpus pinning this site
stops.campa: At twenty-five past three in the afternoon Fermi orders the last control rod drawn the final foot, and the neutron counters climb and do not level off. The reaction sustains itself for about four and a half minutes at half a watt before he calls the rod back in. Forty-nine people are in the room. Eugene Wigner produces a bottle of Chianti and they drink it out of paper cups without a toast. Arthur Compton telephones James Conant at Harvard and says the Italian navigator has landed in the New World, and Conant asks how the natives were.
stops.quote: The Italian navigator has landed in the New World.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Arthur Compton, telephoning James Conant, 2 December 1942; repeated in popular chronicles of the Manhattan Project, no primary transcript located
suggested_refs: Gary Sheahan's 1957 painting of the pile going critical; the 1952 and 1967 plaques on the site
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum, 'Enrico Fermi'

stops.name: X-10, Oak Ridge: the graphite reactor
stops.date_confidence: attested; the coordinate is the X-10 reactor itself, correcting the pool's generic Oak Ridge figures
stops.campa: The pilot plant for plutonium goes critical at the Clinton Engineer Works in the Tennessee ridges, eleven months after the squash court and at a thousand times the power. Fermi is present for the startup with Arthur Compton. The machine is his pile made industrial: air-cooled, loaded by hand from a working face, built to prove the new element can be bred in quantity before the money is poured into Hanford. Oak Ridge is by now a city of tens of thousands of people that did not exist in 1942 and appears on no published map.
suggested_refs: The X-10 Graphite Reactor, Oak Ridge, preserved as a National Historic Landmark

stops.name: United States, the naturalization
stops.date_confidence: July 1944 attested, day not established; the coordinate is the geographic centre of the United States, a deliberate placeholder, since the court where the oath was taken is not named in the sources reached
stops.campa: Fermi and Laura take the oath of citizenship at the earliest date the residence requirement allows, five and a half years after landing. Until this month the man directing the country's reactor programme has been, in law, an enemy alien, subject to travel restrictions that his own military escorts quietly ignore. Italy has surrendered, Benito Mussolini has been deposed, taken off a mountain by German paratroopers and installed in a puppet republic on Lake Garda. Two months later Fermi goes to Los Alamos.
suggested_refs: Fermi's certificate of naturalization, July 1944

stops.name: Los Alamos, F Division
stops.date_confidence: Wikipedia gives September 1944, the Atomic Heritage Foundation gives 16 July 1944; the contradiction is recorded, not resolved, and the coordinate is the canonical Los Alamos pin inherited from robert_oppenheimer.journey.json
stops.campa: Fermi comes onto the mesa as associate director of Project Y and head of F Division, F for Fermi, the division that takes the problems no other division owns. Robert Oppenheimer runs the town. Niels Bohr moves through it under the name Nicholas Baker; Richard Feynman, Hans Bethe and Emilio Segre from Via Panisperna are all inside the fence. The family lives in a house on the mesa like everyone else. He is used here as Rome used him, as the man a problem goes to when the answer is needed before the theory can be finished.
suggested_refs: F Division, Project Y, Los Alamos, 1944-1945
sources: robert_oppenheimer.journey.json, stop 'The secret city: six thousand behind the wire'

stops.name: B Reactor, Hanford: the first slug
stops.date_confidence: Wikipedia's Fermi article says only September 1944; the B Reactor article gives 13 September for first loading and 26 September for criticality; the Atomic Heritage Foundation says 27 September, which falls after criticality and so cannot be the first slug; whether the ceremonial slug was Fermi's own hand is unconfirmed
stops.campa: On the Columbia River in eastern Washington stands the first full-scale plutonium reactor, water-cooled, scaled up from the squash-court pile by DuPont engineers by a factor of a thousand. Fermi is handed the first uranium slug and pushes it into the loading face. Days after startup the reactor poisons itself as fission products accumulate and dies; the spare tubes John Wheeler had insisted be designed into it are loaded, and it comes back. The sources disagree about the day and about whose hand held the slug, and the disagreement is left standing.
suggested_refs: The B Reactor at Hanford, preserved within the Manhattan Project National Historical Park

stops.name: Trinity, the strips of paper
stops.date_confidence: attested; the coordinate is Trinity ground zero in the Jornada del Muerto, correcting the pool's Alamogordo figures, which lie some sixty miles away
stops.campa: Fermi watches from base camp, ten miles from the tower, face down until the flash. When the blast wave arrives he is standing with a handful of torn paper, dropping the scraps from about six feet and watching where they come down. The shift is about two and a half metres. From that number, on the spot, before a single instrument is read, he puts the yield at ten thousand tons of TNT. The instruments will later say more than twice as much. He files a written report the following day in the flattest prose available to him, as though describing weather.
stops.quote: The shift was about 2 1/2 meters, which, at the time, I estimated to correspond to the blast that would be produced by ten thousand tons of T.N.T.
stops.quote_source: Enrico Fermi, 'My Observations during the Explosion at Trinity,' 16 July 1945
suggested_refs: Fermi's typed Trinity observation report, Los Alamos, 16 July 1945

stops.name: Los Alamos, the departure at year's end
stops.date_confidence: attested to the end of 1945
stops.campa: Fermi leaves the mesa on the last day of 1945 with his family and a Medal for Merit. He has sat on the scientific panel that advised the government no technical demonstration would end the war, and he does not write about that afterward, or about Hiroshima, or about Nagasaki, in any text that has been found. Chicago is waiting: a house in Hyde Park, an institute being built around his name, and the physics he actually wants next, which is cosmic rays and the pion.
suggested_refs: The Interim Committee scientific panel report, June 1945

stops.name: Institute for Nuclear Studies, Chicago: the Swift chair
stops.date_confidence: the appointment is dated 1 July 1945, though he is at Los Alamos until December and only takes up the work in 1946; the coordinate corrects the pool's figures by about 370 metres
stops.campa: The University of Chicago names Fermi Charles H. Swift Distinguished Service Professor and builds an Institute for Nuclear Studies around the men who came for the pile and are willing to stay. On 1 July 1946 the Metallurgical Laboratory is reorganised as Argonne National Laboratory, the reactor work going out to the forest preserve where the pile was supposed to have been built in the first place. Fermi teaches. His Chicago doctoral students include Chen-Ning Yang, Tsung-Dao Lee, Owen Chamberlain, Jack Steinberger, Jerome Friedman and Richard Garwin.
suggested_refs: The Institute for Nuclear Studies, University of Chicago, founded 1945

stops.name: Washington, the General Advisory Committee and the Super
stops.date_confidence: the GAC report is dated 30 October 1949 and Fermi sits on the committee from 1946 to 1950; the exact wording of the minority annex could not be re-verified this session, the two Wikipedia GAC pages returning 404
stops.campa: Asked whether the United States should race for a thermonuclear weapon after the Soviet test, the Atomic Energy Commission's advisory committee answers no. Fermi and Isidor Rabi attach a minority annex in language neither man uses anywhere else in his career, calling the weapon an evil thing in any light and its use a policy of exterminating civilian populations, and urging that other nations be asked to renounce it first. Truman orders the crash programme three months later. Fermi goes back to Los Alamos in the summers and works on it.
suggested_refs: The GAC report of 30 October 1949 and the Fermi-Rabi minority annex
sources: Atomic Heritage Foundation / Nuclear Museum (committee service noted, H-bomb detail absent)
standard histories of the AEC General Advisory Committee

stops.name: Los Alamos, the question at lunch
stops.date_confidence: traditional; the conversation is placed in the summer of 1950 and survives only in the recollections of Teller, York and Konopinski, collected by Eric Jones in 1985, thirty-five years later; the month is defaulted to 01
stops.campa: Walking to lunch with Edward Teller, Herbert York and Emil Konopinski, the talk is of a New Yorker cartoon about flying saucers and of whether faster-than-light travel is possible. The subject changes. Partway through the meal Fermi asks, out of nothing, where everybody is. He then estimates aloud, in the manner he taught his students to estimate anything, how many civilisations the galaxy should carry and how long a spacefaring one would need to cross it, and finds the silence hard to account for. No transcript exists.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Fermi at Los Alamos, summer 1950; reconstructed from the recollections of Teller, York and Konopinski in Eric Jones, 'Where Is Everybody? An Account of Fermi's Question,' Los Alamos LA-10311-MS (1985)
suggested_refs: Eric M. Jones, Where Is Everybody? An Account of Fermi's Question, LA-10311-MS (1985)

stops.name: Villa Monastero, Varenna: the last lectures
stops.date_confidence: July 1954; the Italian Physical Society treats this as the school's founding session, but the conference centre at Villa Monastero was created in 1953, so the school was not founded that summer, and Wikipedia does not itself document Fermi's lectures there; contradiction recorded
stops.campa: Fermi comes back to Italy for the summer school on Lake Como and lectures on pions and nucleons to a room of young Italians, some of whom were children when he left. He walks the lake path in the mornings and answers questions on anything put to him. He is visibly ill and says nothing about it. Within the year the school is renamed the International School of Physics Enrico Fermi. From Varenna he goes home to Chicago, where exploratory surgery in October finds a stomach cancer already past operating, and the surgeons close him again.
suggested_refs: Villa Monastero, Varenna, seat of the Scuola Internazionale di Fisica Enrico Fermi

stops.campa: Fermi dies of stomach cancer on 28 November, fifty-three years old, not quite twelve years after the pile went critical a few streets from this door. The tradition among his colleagues is that in the last weeks he timed the drip of his own intravenous feeding with a stopwatch. Laura Fermi outlives him by twenty-three years and writes the household's account of the whole road from Via Panisperna. The house near the Hyde Park campus carries no plaque and is not a city landmark; the claim that it was preserved as one does not survive checking.

stops.name: Enewetak Atoll, element one hundred in the fallout
stops.date_confidence: the Ivy Mike test is 1 November 1952; the identification of fermium in the debris is made in December 1952 at Berkeley, so the stop is dated to the test that produced the material and the pool's conflation of the two dates is corrected
stops.campa: The first thermonuclear device, the weapon Fermi's committee had advised against building, vaporises an island of the Enewetak atoll. Filters flown through the cloud carry the debris back to Berkeley, where Albert Ghiorso's group finds in it two elements nobody has ever made: number ninety-nine and number one hundred. The results stay classified for three years. Element one hundred is named fermium, proposed while Fermi is alive and made official after he is dead, and the substance of it exists nowhere on earth outside the ash of the thing he opposed.

stops.campa: Less than a year after the funeral the Institute for Nuclear Studies is renamed the Enrico Fermi Institute for Nuclear Studies, shortened in 1968 to the Enrico Fermi Institute. The name goes on spreading: an accelerator laboratory on the Illinois prairie, a nuclear generating station on Lake Erie, a gamma-ray telescope in orbit, a paradox about the silence of the galaxy, and every particle in the universe that obeys the exclusion principle, which is to say all the matter there is. stops.campa: The Institute of Physics on the Viminale hill, where the boys of Via Panisperna slowed neutrons with a block of wax in 1934, now houses the Enrico Fermi Museum and the research centre that carries his name. Gianni Amelio films the group's story in 1989 as I ragazzi di via Panisperna, and it ends where the history ends: Ettore Majorana walks off a ship in 1938 and is never found, Bruno Pontecorvo goes to Moscow in 1950, the rest go to America, and the garden with the goldfish pond stays where it was.
